question: A neonate appears irritable and refuses to feed. The patient is febrile and physical examination reveals a bulge at the anterior fontanelle. A CSF culture yields Gram-negative bacilli that form a metallic green sheen on eosin methylene blue (EMB) agar. The virulence factor most important to the development of infection in this patient is:?
analysis: The presence of Gram-negative bacilli forming a metallic green sheen on EMB agar suggests the organism is likely Escherichia coli. In this case, the most important virulence factor contributing to infection is the LPS endotoxin, which is a major component of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria and plays a key role in the pathogenesis of sepsis and septic shock.
